prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1431; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's counsel after a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. Injury described as neck and back strain. Initial file opened and all further contact to be routed through counsel.

Entry 2: Reviewed the insured's policy and confirmed the driver involved is named on it. Coverage was in force at the time of loss, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and describes the lane-change contact between the two cars.

Entry 4: Took the recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matched the first report in every detail.

Entry 5: Spoke with the other driver, who independently described the same lane change and contact between the vehicles. Their account agrees with the claimant's.

Entry 6: Reviewed the scene photographs and two witness statements. Both witnesses and the images are consistent with the sideswipe as described.

Entry 7: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. The damage pattern along the side panels lines up with the impact described, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or records.

Entry 8: Received the medical records from the treating provider. The neck and back strain diagnosis fits the kind and force of a side impact at this speed, and no prior injury to those body areas is on file.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and follow-up visits. The provider's notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of visits tapered as the claimant recovered.

Entry 10: Counsel confirmed the claimant has been attending the scheduled therapy and that the remaining symptoms are mild. Requested updated treatment notes to confirm the current status.

Entry 11: Reviewed the updated notes. Treatment has tapered to periodic check-ins, consistent with the expected recovery timeline for this type of strain.

Entry 12: File assessed as consistent across liability, damage, and injury sources. Recommend proceeding to evaluation of the bodily injury claim through counsel.
